findings.reason: the honest change is a fourth item tuple and a fourth prompt loader in `review.py`, not a parallel module.
findings.text: §6 adds `reckon/crew/figure_review.py` and `reckon/crew/prompts/figure-review.md`, a fourth review kind kept out of the module that already owns review kinds; `review.py` holds `REVIEW_ITEMS` (line 100), `PLAN_REVIEW_ITEMS` (line 147), `PLAN_DESIGN_REVIEW_ITEMS` (line 157) and the per-kind prompt loaders at lines 263-273, so the owner of "what checks does this review kind answer" is that module.

findings.reason: a figure subject on the existing dispatcher deletes the wrapper entirely.
findings.text: the dispatch path at line 2464 (`dispatch_subject = record["subject"] ...`) and the subject branch at line 2269 (`if record.get("subject") == "plan"`) already select the review kind and route it to a recorder; §6's `figure_review.py` would simply call through to that path, adding no behaviour the existing subject dispatcher lacks.

findings.reason: a second registry of review kinds is the fork the duplicate_owner item exists to catch, and it names the file to extend.
findings.text: `_REPORT_RUBRIC_ITEMS` (line 687) maps a review kind to its item tuple and is the registry a new kind belongs in; §6 introduces its own module beside it rather than adding a kind, giving two places that answer "which checklist does this review use".

findings.reason: folding it into `review.py` as a kind removes a module that would hide nothing and keeps the figure checklist in the one place the other checklists live.
findings.text: the module §6 proposes carries only a prompt path, a subject selector and a call to the existing dispatcher and store, which is smaller than the interface it presents; the described figure judgement is visual prose that belongs in a prompt, not behind a module.

findings.reason: citing the owner would convert a new module into an extension, which is the difference the reuse_search item exists to force.
findings.text: §6's prior-art account names no existing review kind; the codebase already reviews three kinds (code, plan content, plan design review) through one schema and one store, and §6 does not say why a figure review is a different shape rather than a fourth kind.

rubric_items.deep_module: a finding — §6's proposed `reckon/crew/figure_review.py` hides little: its judgement is prose in a prompt file, its dispatch delegates to `recovery.dispatch_review_for_run`, and its record goes to the existing review store, so it adds surface rather than depth.
rubric_items.duplicate_owner: a finding — the review-kind owner is `reckon/crew/review.py` (item tuples and per-kind prompt loaders) plus `reckon/crew/recovery.py` (`dispatch_review_for_run` and its subject branch), with the report store and rubric registry in `reckon/crew/plan_review.py`; §6 forks that owner rather than extending it.
rubric_items.reuse_search: a finding — §2 and §3 clearly cite the machinery the plan extends (the §3 reflex reuses `resumption.sweep` and `dispatch_awaiting_reviews`; §2 reuses the existing scope, impl-move and negative-control refusals), but §6 proposes a new review module and prompt without naming the existing review-kind mechanism it most resembles.
rubric_items.thin_wrapper: a finding — `figure_review.py` is a thin layer over the review-subject dispatch that already exists, and the plan does not say why that mechanism cannot carry a fourth review kind instead.
